alignments.note: Preposition fused with its construct noun into one English word, headed on the construct (rules 30, 23).
Construct noun with a supplied 'the', no article morpheme standing in the chain (rule 29).
Finite verb rendered by copula plus adjective; head on the lexical word (rules 24, 44).
Waw takes the 'And' written for it (rule 14).

Preposition fused with its construct noun (rules 30, 23), heading the predicate of the second colon's verbless clause. The italic 'goeth' is the linking verb the ASV writes where a copula would stand — rule 20 names 'come' among them and gives the 'come alike' of `הַכֹּל כַּאֲשֶׁר לַכֹּל` to the predicate morpheme — so it joins this predicate's unit under rule 49, exactly as rule 30's `לִפְנֵי` → *was before* carries a construction-supplied copula without defeating the one-rendering condition. Discontinuous around 'honor' under rule 25; the head stays on the word carrying the relation. Rule 20's subtraction decides it: dropping 'goeth' removes the English link, not a predication, since 'before honor' is written and no participant is added. Marking the italic 'goeth' added under rule 34's supplied-lexical-verb clause was the competing reading (rule 8).
Noun, the subject of the verbless second colon.

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment marked the italic 'goeth' added under rule 34. But rule 34's supplied-lexical-verb clause governs a line whose predicate the Hebrew leaves unwritten altogether, as its 'cheweth' does; here לִפְנֵי כָבוֹד is a written prepositional predicate and 'goeth' merely links עֲנָוָה to it, adding no participant, which is rule 20's expanded copula and rule 49's placement of it on the preposition.
The verb of the first colon is יִגְבַּהּ, rendered 'is haughty', so 'goeth' is not a second realization of a written verb under rule 34's pro-verb sentence either.
